title: The Growing Rectangle: Product Rule Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
A rectangle is 4 cm wide and 3 cm tall. Its width grows 2 cm every second and its height grows 3 cm every second. Does the area grow by 2 × 3 = 6 every second? No: it grows at 18, and faster each second. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 12, Limits and Derivatives) we learn the algebra of derivatives: the sum, product and quotient rules.

You will watch two water tanks show the sum rule, then the rectangle grow live: a strip along the top, a strip down the side and a tiny corner that vanishes as the moment shrinks. That picture gives the product rule (uv)' = u'v + uv', which NCERT calls the Leibnitz rule. A pizza shared among friends explains the quotient rule (u/v)' = (u'v - uv')/v², and we use the power rule for x to the power n. A side-by-side of sum and product, a pause-and-think question, a worked example checked on the graph, the exam trap about the order in the quotient rule, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.
